Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph 06 SEP OILG OPINION NO. MR. ROMULO R. LEUTERIO Lot No. A-138, Brgy. Sapang I Ternate, Cavite Dear Mr. Leuterio: S. 20B This has reference to your letter dated 6 June 2019, requesting the Department's legal opinion on the following queries, quoted hereunder in toto: 1. 2. 4. Was the Liga ng Barangay Resolution #06-S-2010 rightfully done to our property? Our property obtained its judicial title of OCT 0-1911 on 1980 that was made to TCT T-293007 on 1991. The resolution was made on April 27, 2010. We have secure ownership a long time ago prior to any resolution. Does prior rights apply? We cannot acquire a no objection and Brgy. Clearance for business from Barangay Sapang I but during (Ricky Diones) his reign as the Brgy. Captain, he manage to quarry a mountainous area besides the Governor's Drive (national highway), "talipapa" of Sapang I and just across the road is the Elementary School of Sapang. He manage to use his power without any permit to quarry this mountainous land. Based on Sangguniang Panlalawigan Ordinance #8 dated August 23, 1990 that was ratified on April 14, 1991 that Sapang II was created and it was taken from the land boundaries of Sapang I. That we live in our property TCT T-293007, that we are voters of Sapang II, that Sapang II is the one giving us residential certificate but when it comes to business clearance like no objection for quarry and for the lease of property we need to take it from Sapang I. The distance of our property with the Brgy. Of Sapang II is 129.75 meters compare to the distance of our property to Brgy. Sapang I which is 971.45 meters. What really should be followed based on the ordinance above? We did acquire different permit application documents on different government agencies like ECC from DENR, EMB CALABARZON 4A, Certificate of Zoning from MPDC, adjacent lot owners, zoning and current tax declaration from municipality of Ternate, Certificate of no Objection of parks and wildlife clearance from DENR Lands CALABARZON, certificate of no objection from TIEZA, and no objection from national historical commission. All of this wasted because after acquiring all of this the Barangay of Sapang I neglect to give us no

objection without even answering our request. What is the remedy on all this? At the outset, the Department finds that Mr. Ricky Diones is no longer the Punong Barangay of Brgy. Sapang I, hence, administrative complaint pursuant to the Local Government Code is no longer a remedy against him. However, civil or criminal actions may be filed against him. On the first query, as explicitly provided in Section 2(f), Article VI of the 2016 Constitution and By-Laws of the Liga ng mga Barangay sa Pilipinas, one of the duties and functions of the Liga is to adopt measures to promote the welfare of the Barangay Officials. Hence, this level finds that the subject Resolution passed by the Liga ng mga Barangay of Ternate, Cavite may suffer from possible legal infirmity and not within the authority of the Liga to pass as the subject matter thereof does not pertain to the welfare of the barangay officials. It can also be considered as an intrusion to the powers and functions of the Punong Barangay and Members of the Sangguniang Barangay. The second query is a mere narration of facts, thus, we will no longer answer the same. However, if your allegation that Mr. Diones, during his reign has managed to use his power without any permit to quarry this mountainous land can be substantiated by evidence, you can file the appropriate charges pursuant to the penal provisions of Republic Act No. 7942, otherwise, known as "The Philippine Mining Act of 1995". With respect to your third query, upon perusal of the documents attached in your letter, it appears that some of the documents indicate that the location of the property is Brgy. Sapang I and some indicate Brgy. Sapang II. Moreover, the Department was not furnished with a copy of the subject Sangguniang Panlalawigan Ordinance No. 8 dated August 23, 1990. Thus, we are constrained from answering your query as the subject ordinance cannot be properly evaluated/assessed by the Department. Nevertheless, please be advised that what barangays can issue is "barangay clearance", not "business clearance". Be that as it may, Republic Act No. 11032, otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018", has already provided for the so-called "Business One Stop Shop (BOSS)", wherein, a single common site or location, or a single online website or portal is already designated for the Business Permit and Licensing System (BPLS) of an LGU (Cities/MunicipaIities) to receive and process applications, receive payments, and issue approved licenses, clearances, permits, or authorizations. On the fourth query, if it is your belief that your rights have been violated by the concerned officials, may we advise you to file an appropriate complaint in

accordance with Sections 601 and 612 of the Local Government Code or Republic Act No. 6770, otherwise known as the "Ombudsman Act of 1989". We hope we have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: M IN B. DINO ndersecretary CC: Dir. Manuel Q. Gotis, CESO 111 Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A (CALABARZON) Ls/90V 1 SECTION 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. - An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: (a) Disloyalty to the Republic of the Philippines; (b) Culpable violation of the Constitution; (c) Dishonesty, oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; (e) Abuse of authority; (f) Unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive working days, except in the case of members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, Sangguniang bayan, and Sangguniang Barangay; (g) Application for, or acquisition Of, foreign citizenship or residence or the status of an immigrant of another country; and (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. 2 SECTION 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office Of the President; and (c) A complaint against any elective Barangay official shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory.
